note: The review-and-choose board. Every row is a proposal, not a change: nothing here is implemented until the owner records a choice. Rows are ordered by the sequence in which they can be done — a row whose 'depends_on' is not resolved yet is shown as blocked, and the reason is named. 'cost' and 'risk' are the reviewer's estimates, deliberately coarse, and are labelled as estimates; they are not program facts. Rows marked 'implemented_this_session' were safe, additive, inside this session's own file scope, and are published here so the owner can see exactly what was done on their behalf.

status_vocabulary.awaiting_owner_decision: Proposal published; the owner has not chosen an option.
status_vocabulary.blocked_on_information: Cannot be decided until the named gap in gaps.json is closed.
status_vocabulary.implemented_this_session: Additive change inside this session's own scope, already shipped in this pull request, listed here for review and reversible.
status_vocabulary.recommended_do_nothing: Considered and rejected; recorded so the question is not reopened by the next session.

recommendations.title: Make the tables exist before JavaScript runs
recommendations.suggestion: Pre-render the row markup into the HTML at build time from ledger/*.json, and let the script enhance it instead of creating it. No new data source is needed — the rows already exist in the ledger and the renderers already exist in assets/js/app.js.

options.label: Pre-render every root page at build time
options.tradeoff: Largest gain, changes every root page and the CI baseline. Reuses ledger data; no value changes.

options.label: Promote pages/ to the landing and retire the JS shell from the home page
options.tradeoff: Fastest single change; collapses two namespaces into one and forces the A-06 decision early.

options.label: Add a <noscript> summary table only
options.tradeoff: Cheap and honest, but a crawler that renders nothing still sees one summary, not the record.

recommendations.why: It is the only option that fixes the defect without discarding the ledger-first architecture, and it removes the 102 KB data payload from the critical path at the same time (A-09).
recommendations.cost: estimate: 1–2 sessions of work in tools/ + regenerated output
recommendations.risk: estimate: low — every value still comes from the ledger; the gate that compares committed HTML to the ledger must be re-baselined once.

recommendations.title: Put the sentence where the links are
recommendations.suggestion: Render the required sentence immediately above the first affiliate link on every page that carries one, in the visual weight of a lead-in rather than a footnote, and keep the footer copy as well.

options.label: Disclosure block above the first link, repeated in the footer
options.tradeoff: Satisfies both the programme wording and the FTC 'hard to miss' test. Slightly more visual space on short pages.

options.label: Link-level label on every affiliate anchor as well ('paid link')
options.tradeoff: Strongest reading of the FTC guidance; adds noise next to 600+ links.

options.label: Leave as is
options.tradeoff: Defensible on section 5's wording, but the site's own rule R-02 and the FTC brochure both argue against a footer-only disclosure. Not recommended.

recommendations.why: The sentence itself is already correct and verified; only its position is wrong. Option A fixes position without touching the wording the Operating Agreement requires.
recommendations.cost: estimate: under an hour of generator work plus regeneration

recommendations.title: Give the root pages the head tags marketing/ already has
recommendations.suggestion: Add rel="canonical", an Open Graph block and one JSON-LD block per root page, generated from the same page registry that writes the titles.

options.label: Canonical + OG only
options.tradeoff: Cheap, no risk of misdescribing the page.

options.label: Canonical + OG + JSON-LD
options.tradeoff: More surface for rich results, but structured data must be true; a Product block without a price or rating is a thin block and Google's merchant-listing guidance expects real values.

options.label: Do nothing until the public page set is decided (A-06)
options.tradeoff: Avoids stamping canonicals on pages that may be archived. Slower.

recommendations.why: Canonical and OG are safe on any page set; JSON-LD should wait for the A-06 decision, because structured data on a page that is later archived is wasted work.
recommendations.risk: estimate: low; a wrong canonical is worse than none, so it must be generated, never typed

recommendations.title: Qualify the 150 unqualified Amazon links
recommendations.suggestion: Apply rel="sponsored noopener noreferrer" to every Amazon anchor outside a source-citation cell, using the helper that already exists in assets/js/app.js, and extend the CI assertion beyond pages/.

options.label: Qualify all of them, leave citation cells alone
options.tradeoff: Matches Google's guidance and the README's own claim. Citation cells stay clean for audit legibility.

options.label: Qualify every Amazon anchor including citation cells
options.tradeoff: Maximally consistent, but a review page where every evidence link is sponsored reads oddly to a human auditor.

options.label: Leave as is and correct the README
options.tradeoff: Honest, but the links themselves remain unqualified where Google asks for qualification.

recommendations.why: It makes the published claim true, it is mechanical, and it needs no data change.

recommendations.title: Decide whether the site measures anything at all
recommendations.suggestion: Pick one measurement posture and publish it. The site currently describes tracking, conversion analysis and campaign optimization in detail while measuring nothing.

options.label: No measurement until an Associates account exists
options.tradeoff: Zero privacy surface, zero data. The optimization pages become explicitly 'planned' rather than 'available'.

options.label: First-party click counter on a host the owner controls
options.tradeoff: Real outbound-click counts, no cookies or visitor ids (the schema in tools/tracking_schema.sql already assumes this). Needs hosting and a privacy statement.

options.label: Third-party analytics
options.tradeoff: Fastest to read, largest privacy and consent surface, and it introduces the only third-party script on the site.

recommendations.why: Until an Associates tag exists (SA-03), a click count cannot be tied to a commission, so the cheapest correct posture is to measure nothing and say so. Option B becomes worthwhile on the day the tag exists.
recommendations.cost: estimate: A is copy-only; B is one session plus hosting
recommendations.risk: estimate: A none; B low if the no-visitor-identifier rule is kept

recommendations.title: One public site, one page per reader intent
recommendations.suggestion: Publish one reader-facing site (marketing/ is the closest to ready), keep the evidence namespaces as a clearly labelled archive, and stop publishing seven parallel descriptions of three products.

options.label: marketing/ becomes the public site; the rest move under /archive/ with noindex
options.tradeoff: Biggest ranking and clarity gain. Requires the archive to be routed and the sitemap rebuilt; nothing is deleted.

options.label: Keep everything, add noindex to the duplicate namespaces
options.tradeoff: Smaller change, keeps every URL working. The origin still hosts seven descriptions, one of which is the reader-facing one.

options.label: Do nothing
options.tradeoff: The site continues to present the exact shape Google's scaled-content and thin-affiliation sections describe. Not recommended.

recommendations.why: It gets the ranking benefit of a single public site without deleting work six sessions produced, and it is reversible in one commit. Option A can follow once the owner has looked at the archive.
recommendations.risk: estimate: medium — every namespace has its own gates and relative asset paths; each must be checked after the move

recommendations.title: Name the person responsible
recommendations.suggestion: Publish a named author or editor, an About page that states the verification method in plain language, and a visible 'last reviewed' date on every editorial page.

options.label: Real named owner as author, About page, per-article review date
options.tradeoff: The single highest-trust change available. Requires the owner to accept being named.

options.label: Site-level authorship only ('the Counter Notes desk'), no personal name
options.tradeoff: Cheaper and still better than silence; weaker than a person for Google's authorship signals.

options.label: No byline
options.tradeoff: Maintains the current gap. Google's own site-reputation example treats an unauthored affiliate article as likely to draw action.

recommendations.why: It is the only option that answers the question Google's guidance asks first, and it is free.
recommendations.cost: estimate: under an hour once the owner says yes
recommendations.risk: estimate: none technical; reputational if the named person is not real

recommendations.title: Put something real on the page
recommendations.suggestion: Add photographs — of the owner's own units where they exist, or manufacturer imagery under the Associates IP licence attached to a tagged link.

options.label: Owner's own photographs, dated and captioned as such
options.tradeoff: Strongest evidence available and the only route to first-hand claims. Requires the owner to own or borrow the products.

options.label: Manufacturer imagery used under the IP licence with a corresponding Special Link
options.tradeoff: Available today; it is not evidence of testing and must not be captioned as if it were.

options.label: No imagery
options.tradeoff: Keeps the site text-only; forfeits social cards, image search and every 'show your experience' signal.

recommendations.why: It is achievable without a purchase and is legal under the licence the project is already governed by; A should be layered on top whenever the owner has the products in hand.
recommendations.cost: estimate: under an hour plus asset work
recommendations.risk: estimate: low if each image sits next to a tagged link, as Trademark Guideline 1 requires

recommendations.title: Cut the 472 KB the landing page needs before it renders
recommendations.suggestion: Drop the 102 KB data script from the critical path (R-01 does this for free), subset the two font families to the weights actually used, and preload only the face used above the fold.

options.label: Fix after R-01, then subset fonts
options.tradeoff: Sequenced correctly: most of the weight disappears with the rendering fix.

options.label: Subset fonts now
options.tradeoff: Independent of R-01 and safe; roughly two-thirds of the font bytes can go.

options.label: Leave as is
options.tradeoff: 472 KB to render an empty table on a phone.

recommendations.why: It can be done independently of the bigger rendering decision, and it is measurable before and after.
recommendations.risk: estimate: low; re-render the pages and compare the visual result

recommendations.title: Say which URLs are public
recommendations.suggestion: Declare the public page set once, generate one sitemap from it, and make every other namespace's status explicit (archive, noindex, or internal evidence).

options.label: One generated sitemap from a declared public set
options.tradeoff: The crawler's view matches the intent. Needs the A-06 decision first.

options.label: Keep two sitemaps, expand the root one to cover the public set
options.tradeoff: Less invasive; keeps marketing/'s self-contained sitemap.

options.label: Leave as is
options.tradeoff: 16 of 114 URLs declared — the site tells Google everything else is accidental.

recommendations.why: Two sitemaps on one origin is the same ambiguity as two 'products' pages, one level up.
recommendations.cost: estimate: under an hour after A-06

recommendations.title: Make every title unique and short
recommendations.suggestion: Add the category or page qualifier to the four duplicated titles and trim the 14 titles over 60 characters in the generator, not in the HTML.

options.label: Fix in the generator
options.tradeoff: Permanent, and the gate that compares output to the ledger keeps it fixed.

options.label: Hand-edit the four pages
options.tradeoff: Faster today; the next regeneration removes it.

recommendations.why: The generators own these files; a hand edit is undone by the next build.

recommendations.title: Make CI able to see what this audit saw
recommendations.suggestion: Add four checks to the deploy workflow: CSS url() resolution, disclosure-before-first-affiliate-link, rel=sponsored outside pages/, and sitemap coverage of the declared public set.

options.label: Add all four
options.tradeoff: A regression in any of them fails the build rather than shipping. A little slower CI.

options.label: Add the two cheapest now (CSS url(), disclosure position)
options.tradeoff: Immediate coverage of the two defects that actually shipped this week.

options.label: Add none
options.tradeoff: The suite remains strong on provenance and blind to presentation regressions.

recommendations.why: Two of the four are implemented and tested in this session (tools/check_css_urls.py, tools/validate_audit.py); the other two need the page set and the disclosure markup decided first.
recommendations.cost: estimate: B is already done and wired; A is another session
recommendations.risk: estimate: low — each new check must be negative-tested before it is trusted, as the existing gates were
recommendations.decision: partial: tools/check_css_urls.py and tools/validate_audit.py are wired into CI in this pull request; the sponsored-link and sitemap checks remain open

recommendations.title: Settle the Associates account before any further build work
recommendations.suggestion: The only item that blocks revenue is not technical. Confirm the account, the marketplace, the Associate ID, and whether a github.io address satisfies the site-ownership test before generating a single tagged link.

options.label: Owner confirms the account and supplies the tag out of band, then the site switches on
options.tradeoff: Unblocks everything; requires the owner to act.

options.label: Build the tagged-link switch now and ship it dark
options.tradeoff: The site is ready the day the tag exists; the placeholder must be unable to resolve to a live link before approval.

options.label: Continue building content without the account
options.tradeoff: Does not block growth of the archive, but the site cannot earn and the optimization pages stay theoretical.

recommendations.why: Everything the brief asks for downstream of revenue — tracking, optimization, campaign learning — is inert without an approved tag.

recommendations.title: Keep the one writing rule that separates this site from the category
recommendations.suggestion: Publish the editorial rule the better pages already follow — no first-hand claim without a dated record, no superlative without the spec that supports it, no number without a source — as a public page, and lint every future article against it. Do not generate volume to fill a content calendar.

options.label: Public editorial standard + lint
options.tradeoff: Slow to fill a calendar, hard to dispute, and it is the one claim a competitor cannot copy quickly.

options.label: Keep the rule internal
options.tradeoff: Less exposure; the reader has to take the site's word for it.

options.label: Publish more articles at a faster rate
options.tradeoff: The pattern Google's scaled-content section describes. Not recommended.

recommendations.why: The site's differentiator is not the products, it is the refusal to assert unverified things; publishing that rule turns an internal discipline into a visible reason to trust the page.
